key_insight: Recent rollouts for the same prompt provide reusable n-gram drafts that accelerate RL post-training without an auxiliary model while preserving the rollout distribution through target-model verification.
engineering_relevance: NgramRL targets the autoregressive rollout bottleneck, which can exceed 70% of training time, without requiring drafter training or persistent GPU-resident drafter state.
method: Build per-prompt n-gram draft caches from bounded recent rollout histories.
Verify drafts with the target model to preserve the rollout distribution.
Adaptively prefetch likely verification outcomes under a candidate budget, falling back to sequential lookup for uncovered outcomes.
evidence_signal: Across two model families and three workloads, warm-cache NgramRL commits 3.60–7.77 tokens per target forward; on Spider, prefetching delivers 1.38× measured rollout throughput over synchronous NgramRL.
watch_item: Reported token-efficiency gains are from the warm-cache regime; cold starts or limited repetition across rollouts may reduce benefits.
paper_title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
